fieldChanges.before:
**Programs and Services**
One Small Step’s Clothes Cabin gives free clothing, shoes, household linens and hygiene items. Back to Work helps with required workwear and a pair of work shoes for a new job. Unsheltered clients can also use showers, weekly laundry, lockers and mailboxes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For anyone who cannot afford the items needed. Clothing visits are once every three months, for yourself, your partner and your children under 18. Bring current photo ID of any kind; ask about a temporary accommodation if you are obtaining ID. Work items require new-hire papers, an employer letter or the Back to Work request form. Staff may ask for guardianship information when you collect clothing for children.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit during client hours; no appointment or referral is needed. For a new job, bring its clothing requirements and employment evidence. For help, call 480-285-4111 or email info@onesmallstepaz.org.

**Access**
The building is at the back of the business park. Children cannot enter the shopping area; if they come, they must stay in the small playroom or lobby. Arrive at least one hour before closing for showers and two hours before closing for laundry.

**Important Information to Know**
Quantities depend on stock. The FAQ usually allows 4–7 clothing items plus socks and underwear, and one set of sheets, one blanket or one set of towels per visit; ask about that day’s limits. Clothes Cabin closes for holidays, the day before Thanksgiving, the Christmas–New Year week and the last week of January. Donation and paid resale-shop hours differ from free client hours.

fieldChanges.before:
**Programs and Services**
Free job planning, employer referrals, resumes, interview preparation and interview clothing. Uniforms, safety shoes, tools and transportation help may be available; ask about the items and limits.

The separate Workforce Housing program offers 90 days in a private room in shared housing, weekly support and life-skills classes, followed by nine months of follow-up.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Job-search services are free for unemployed or underemployed people. Newly employed assistance generally requires permanent/direct-hire W-2 work, 25–40 hours weekly, at least minimum wage and a start within the past 30 days. Required screenings must be completed. Temporary, seasonal, staffing-agency and app-based jobs do not qualify for that extra assistance.

Workforce Housing has separate rules: applicants must work full time in a direct-hire job earning at least $18 an hour. Ask about current openings and any other requirements; qualifying for job-search help does not qualify someone for housing.

**How to Best Connect**
Walk into 1833 W. Main St., Suite 128, Mesa, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–noon or 1–4 p.m.; closed noon–1 p.m. No appointment is needed. Call 602-755-5627 with questions. Bring photo ID, a phone and a resume if available; ask for help if these are missing.

**Access**
The office is near the Sycamore/Main Street light-rail stop. For newly employed assistance, have the employer email jobs@theworkeraz.org from a company address with your full name, start date, pay and weekly hours. This is separate from starting a job search. For Workforce Housing, ask a housing expert about enrollment, the waiting list, housing location and costs. The Mesa office is not a housing unit.

**Important Information to Know**
The newly employed resources are offered once and depend on supplies. Ask staff which clothing or equipment they can provide before purchasing it. The organization also uses the name St. Joseph the Worker. Housing is a separate program. The site describes low living costs but gives no current amount; ask about rent, deposits and other charges before agreeing to a place. Do not assume the free job-search service means free housing.

fieldChanges.before:
**Programs and Services**
Pays approved refundable security deposits to the landlord. Utility deposits can be requested with the security-deposit application. This is deposit help, not payment of overdue rent or ordinary monthly utility bills.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The new rental unit must be in Mesa. Apply before signing the lease or moving in. The landlord and utility provider must accept the City’s payment guarantee and program terms, and the unit must pass inspection. Ask staff to check the current household-income and residency rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Housing at 480-644-3536 to confirm current intake and funding, then use the program’s online application or ask for a paper form. The linked form asks for photo ID for the household head, Social Security cards for household members, an unsigned proposed lease, income records and two recent full bank statements. Ask for the current checklist and help obtaining missing documents. For utility deposits, get an account and deposit letter from the utility provider.

If you cannot upload documents, the form lists fax 480-644-2923 or the secure drop box at 200 S. Center St., Building 1. Label them with your name and “Security Deposit Application.”

Housing questions can also go to housing.info@mesaaz.gov.

**Access**
Office lobby: Monday–Thursday, 7:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; Housing Specialist visits need an appointment. Ask for help completing the application if needed.

**Important Information to Know**
Start well before the move. The linked form asks for at least 14 days on its first page, says 10 days on its last page, and estimates 10–14 business days to process. Confirm the actual timeline with Housing. Approval also requires inspection; an application is not a promise of payment. Help covers approved refundable deposits, with the rental deposit capped at two months’ rent on the linked form. Utility-deposit help requires rental-deposit approval.
